description: Every acceptance test for the klowb platform. Maintained by hand after initial generation. Rules: never delete an entry; never weaken a description to make it pass; 'passing' requires a last_execution record; 'skipped' is not a valid status.

last_execution_shape.commit: git short sha the run was made on, or null if uncommitted

tests.description: All required brain documents exist and are non-empty (CLAUDE.md, README.md, progress.md, tests.json, docs/architecture.md, docs/data-providers.md, docs/risk-model.md, docs/execution-model.md, docs/security.md, docs/runbook.md, docs/decisions/, docs/BRAIN.md, docs/brief/original-brief.md, docs/plan/phases.md, docs/open-questions.md, docs/architecture/dependency-decisions.md).
tests.json is structurally valid: unique ids, allowed type/status values, required fields present, tests marked passing/failing have a last_execution record and their relevant files exist.
docs/architecture/dependency-decisions.md records every repository URL the brief asks to investigate (18 repositories).

docs/data-providers.md covers every provider the brief names (Alpaca, Twelve Data, Massive, Tiingo, Finnhub, Interactive Brokers, Alpha Vantage, SEC EDGAR, yfinance, Stooq, FRED, ECB, CFTC, Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, CCXT).
progress.md contains the five sections the brief requires: current phase, finished work, unresolved problems, next action, commands used for verification.
Every ADR referenced in docs/BRAIN.md section 5 exists in docs/decisions/.
Every failure-injection case and every financial edge case listed in the brief is covered by at least one acceptance test in tests.json (traceability via the 'covers' field).
No .env or key-like file is tracked by git and .gitignore ignores .env files.
Canonical Observation schemas carry every provenance field from the brief; FeedQuality enum contains exactly the seven required values; DataType discriminates TRADE/QUOTE/BAR/TICKER.
Timestamps: naive datetimes are rejected; timezone-aware non-UTC values are normalised to UTC; serialisation is RFC 3339 UTC.
Price/size validation: zero, negative, NaN and infinite prices are rejected; negative sizes rejected; Decimal precision is preserved for crypto (>= 8 dp) and forex pip/pipette precision.
A crossed quote (bid > ask) is representable and exposes is_crossed; a locked quote exposes is_locked; spread and mid are computed in Decimal.
Bar validation: low <= min(open, close), high >= max(open, close), low <= high, volume >= 0; a zero-volume bar is valid and flagged; is_final defaults to false.

Instrument model: canonical symbol rules per asset class (equity ticker, BASE/QUOTE for crypto and FX), instrument_id format, derivative-ready optional fields default to None, increments must be positive.
Settings: TRADING_MODE defaults to research; live mode with any missing gate fails to load with an explicit error; paper never implies live; unknown modes are rejected.

tests.description: Provider conformance suite: any MarketDataProvider implementation must set provenance fields, use the injected clock, classify errors, expose health and stop cleanly; the mock provider passes it.
Mock provider is deterministic: the same seed and virtual clock produce byte-identical event sequences.
Mock and replay data are always labelled feed_quality=SIMULATED and can never be emitted with another label.
Bar aggregation from trades: correct OHLCV, VWAP and trade count per interval for 1m and higher timeframes.
Bar finality: a bar is emitted as final only after the clock passes the interval end; in-progress bars are flagged is_final=false (no lookahead).
No bars are created across closed periods; a missing candle stays missing unless forward-fill is explicitly configured.
Data quality: stale timestamps (event far behind receipt during an open session) are flagged and surfaced.
Data quality: duplicate events are detected by event identity and dropped idempotently.
Data quality: backwards-time / reordered events are detected; late events within tolerance are re-ordered, beyond tolerance quarantined.
Data quality: missing sequence numbers are detected, counted and trigger a repair request.
Data quality: non-positive and non-finite prices are quarantined with reason and never reach consumers.
Data quality: crossed markets are flagged; persistent crossing on a single-venue feed is quarantined.
Data quality: extreme outliers (robust jump filter) are quarantined, while a genuine large gap confirmed by subsequent prints is accepted and flagged.
Data quality: zero or invalid volume is flagged according to data type.
Data quality: malformed symbols are rejected at normalisation and quarantined.
Data quality: sustained provider latency degradation moves provider health to DEGRADED and raises a stale-feed alert metric.
Token-bucket rate limiter enforces the configured rate and burst using the injected clock.
Retry policy: exponential backoff with full jitter, capped delay, bounded attempts, honours Retry-After; non-retryable error kinds are never retried.
Circuit breaker: closed -> open after threshold failures -> half-open probe after cool-down -> closed on success / open on failure.
Error classification maps HTTP status codes, timeouts, connection errors and malformed payloads to the closed ProviderError kinds with the correct retryable flag.
Equity calendar: regular session open/close for XNYS in UTC; market holiday is closed.
Equity calendar: early-close days end at the early close; premarket and postmarket windows are modelled and distinguishable from the regular session.
Equity calendar across DST transitions: session times stay correct in exchange-local time and shift correctly in UTC.
Crypto calendar is open 24/7 including weekends and holidays.
FX calendar: open from the Sunday open to the Friday close with named session windows (Sydney/Tokyo/London/New York) and correct DST handling.
VirtualClock and SystemClock satisfy the Clock protocol; VirtualClock advances only when told and drives timers deterministically.
Property: for arbitrary valid trade sequences aggregated bars satisfy low <= open,close <= high and volume equals the sum of trade sizes.
Property: the quality service is idempotent - feeding the same event stream twice yields the same accepted set and no duplicates.
Replaying a recorded event file through the full pipeline yields an identical final-state hash on every run.
Replay runs on a virtual clock at any speed with no dependence on wall-clock time; results equal the real-time-paced run.
Quarantined events are persisted with reason, provider, instrument and payload hash and are returned by GET /api/v1/quality/quarantine.
WS /api/v1/stream delivers canonical events with feed-quality metadata to a subscribed client; unsubscribed instruments are not delivered.
GET /api/v1/bars returns bars for an instrument/timeframe/range with pagination and input validation.
GET /api/v1/providers/health returns state, last message age, error counts and circuit state per provider.
GET /api/v1/market/status returns the session state per calendar from the injected clock.
The ingestion supervisor restarts a crashed stream task with bounded backoff and shuts down cleanly on application stop.
WebSocket endpoint rejects disallowed Origins, enforces per-connection subscription limits and disconnects slow consumers.
Injected HTTP 429: the client backs off honouring Retry-After, stays within the attempt budget, and reports rate_limited in health.
Injected HTTP 500s: retried with jitter up to the bound, then the circuit opens and calls fail fast.
Injected timeout: classified as retryable timeout, bounded retries, no hang.
Injected malformed JSON in the stream: the message is quarantined and the stream continues.
Injected WebSocket disconnect: reconnect with bounded jittered backoff, resubscribe, reconnect counter increments, no duplicate bars after resume.
Injected stale, duplicate and reordered events in one stream are each handled per the quality rules and counted in metrics.
Redis unavailable at runtime: the event bus falls back to in-process delivery and the stream keeps working; health reports degraded.
PostgreSQL unavailable at runtime: bar/quarantine writes fail with explicit errors and bounded buffering, live streaming to clients continues, recovery resumes persistence.

Recorded Kraken WS v2 fixtures (status, subscribe ack, ticker snapshot/update, trade snapshot/update, ohlc, heartbeat, pong, error) parse into provider models and map to canonical observations, tolerating unknown fields.
Recorded Kraken REST fixtures (OHLC, AssetPairs, error envelopes) parse correctly; the last OHLC entry is marked not final.
Kraken symbol mapping: canonical BTC/USD <-> WS v2 BTC/USD <-> REST legacy names; unsupported pairs are rejected.
Kraken numeric fields are parsed as Decimal without float rounding (parse_float=Decimal), preserving 8+ decimal places.
Heartbeat watchdog: silence longer than the tolerance forces a reconnect; heartbeats and data both reset the watchdog; an application ping keeps an idle connection alive.

Reconnect policy: immediate bounded retries after a random drop, >= 5 s spacing after maintenance, and a hard attempt budget far below 150 per 10 minutes; exceeding the budget opens the circuit instead of looping.
trade_id gap detection per symbol raises a gap event and requests REST backfill; duplicates after reconnect are dropped.
Kraken system status other than online (maintenance, cancel_only, post_only) marks provider health degraded/down and blocks execution eligibility.
Kraken observations are labelled REALTIME_SINGLE_VENUE with venue KRAKEN, entitlement kraken-public and redistribution_allowed=false.
Subscription failures (success=false) are surfaced as classified errors and do not leave the adapter believing it is subscribed.
Stablecoin depeg detection: a stablecoin quote deviating beyond the configured band from its peg raises a quality flag and marks dependent pairs.
Against a local fake Kraken WS server: connect, receive status, subscribe, stream trades/ticker, build bars, survive a forced disconnect, resubscribe and continue with no duplicate or missing bars.
REST backfill fills the gap after a reconnect and merges with streamed data idempotently.
Kraken provider passes the shared provider conformance suite.
Provider health metrics for Kraken (latency, error rate by kind, reconnects, gaps, last message age) are exported on /metrics and the health API.
Kraken REST backfill under 429, 5xx, timeout and the EAPI:Rate limit exceeded / EService:Throttled error envelopes behaves per the retry policy.
Opt-in live smoke test against the real Kraken public WebSocket: connect, subscribe to BTC/USD, receive status + ticker + trade, clean shutdown. Excluded from default test runs.
PriceChart creates one chart per mount with the v5 API (addSeries with CandlestickSeries/HistogramSeries), removes it on unmount, and never disables the TradingView attribution logo.
Bar-to-chart mapping produces strictly ascending unique UTC-second timestamps, parses Decimal strings safely, and emits whitespace points for closed periods/missing candles.
Live updates call series.update for the latest bar and do not call setData per tick.
Provider health panel renders HEALTHY, DEGRADED, DOWN and UNKNOWN states with text labels and a stale-data warning.
Every price display includes the feed-quality badge; DELAYED shows the delay; SIMULATED and UNOFFICIAL are unmistakable.
Chart text alternative: a screen-reader summary and data table describe the visible range (last, change, high, low, range, feed quality).
Stream hook reconnects with bounded backoff, surfaces connection state, and marks data stale after the freshness threshold.
Market Command Center renders market status, provider health and a candlestick chart with volume from the mock provider.
Switching timeframe reloads bars and updates the chart; the selected timeframe is reflected in the URL.
Loading, error, empty and degraded states are shown for the chart and health panels when the API misbehaves.
Responsive layouts: desktop multi-panel, tablet functional two-column, mobile single-column with only the supported views and no horizontal scroll.
Keyboard-only use reaches every control with a visible focus indicator; prefers-reduced-motion disables animation.
Automated axe scan of the dashboard reports no serious or critical violations.
A live price update streamed over the WebSocket updates the last price and the chart without a page reload.
Frontend error reports are accepted by the API endpoint, rate-limited, size-limited and logged without PII.
Return features (1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, daily) match hand-computed golden values.
Trend features (moving averages, distance from MA, trend slope, breakout distance) match golden values.
Momentum features (ROC, RSI, relative strength, multi-horizon momentum) match golden values.
Volatility features (ATR, realized volatility, Parkinson, Garman-Klass, volatility percentile, compression/expansion) match golden values.
Volume features (relative volume, volume z-score, session VWAP, price/VWAP distance) match golden values; VWAP resets per session.
Market-structure features (gap, prior high/low, opening range, intraday high/low, mechanical support/resistance) match golden values.
Order-flow features (spread, depth, imbalance, aggressive-trade proxy, microprice) are computed only when true quote/book data exists and are otherwise absent, not fabricated.
Cross-asset features (rolling correlation, beta, residual return, index-relative return) match golden values on aligned timestamps.
Feature registry: every feature has a name, version, inputs and warm-up length; a FeatureSnapshot id is a deterministic hash of inputs, feature versions and as-of time.
Features handle zero-volume bars, missing candles and insufficient history by returning NaN/absent with a reason, never a misleading number.
Corporate-action handling in features: split, reverse split and dividend adjustments are applied consistently to return features and never mixed with unadjusted prices.
No-lookahead property for every registered feature: the value at time t is unchanged when data after t is appended or perturbed.
Determinism property: recomputing any feature on the same input gives bit-identical output regardless of batch vs incremental computation.

Stock universe filters: minimum price, minimum ADV, minimum dollar volume, spread threshold, market cap when available, session eligibility, corporate-event flags, borrow availability for shorts when known.
Crypto universe filters: minimum quote volume, exchange status, spread, depth, funding when relevant, stablecoin/quote-currency filters.
Forex universe filters: supported pair, spread, session activity, liquidity proxy.
Universe exclusions: halted and delisted instruments are excluded with an explicit reason; a renamed symbol keeps its history under the stable instrument id.
Multi-stage selection is deterministic, records the reason each instrument was dropped at each stage, and never passes a filtered-out instrument to the expensive (agent) stage.
Replaying the same market data yields identical feature snapshots and an identical selected universe.
Feature snapshots are persisted with their versions and can be reloaded by id; the API exposes the latest snapshot per instrument.
Opportunity model validates direction, horizon, strategy family, expected move/cost/edge in bps, confidence in [0,1], freshness and feed quality.
Net expected edge = gross expected edge minus modelled costs (spread, slippage, commissions, funding, borrow) using the shared cost model.
Scanner ranking is deterministic with explicit tie-breaks; stale candidates and candidates on unhealthy feeds are demoted or excluded with a reason.
Scanner never ranks an instrument that failed universe selection.
GET /api/v1/scanner returns ranked candidates with all required columns, filtering, sorting and pagination.
GET /api/v1/opportunities/{id} returns the idea with entry zone, stop, targets, expected R:R, costs and provenance.
Scanner table renders every required column including the data-feed badge and freshness, and is sortable by keyboard with correct aria-sort.
Scanner page lists ranked candidates, filters by asset class and opens a trade idea detail page.
Trade idea detail shows chart with entry zone, stop and targets, expected R:R, expected costs, and provenance; mobile layout is usable.
AgentSignal contract contains every field from the brief with bounds (probability and confidence in [0,1], non-empty invalidators for directional signals, source ids present).
Routing runs only eligible agents for the asset class, available data, horizon, regime and strategy eligibility; not all agents run for every asset.
Each agent declares one evidence class; correlated agents in the same class are aggregated before cross-class weighting so they are not double-counted.
Ensemble math: agent_edge and ensemble_edge follow the documented formula including cost and uncertainty penalties; golden cases.
Disagreement statistics reduce confidence and size monotonically; abstention occurs only above the extreme threshold; ordinary disagreement never yields NO TRADE.
Reliability history is keyed by agent, asset class, regime, strategy and horizon and is applied only after the minimum observation count; before that a neutral prior is used.
Deterministic agents (momentum, mean reversion, volatility, technical structure, order flow, cross-asset, regime) produce signals solely from the feature snapshot and are reproducible.
MockLLMClient returns deterministic typed outputs from fixtures; LLM-assisted agents validate output against the schema and reject unknown source ids.
Type-level and runtime guarantee: no code path creates an OrderIntent from free-form text; only EnsembleDecision objects can produce one.
Adversarial critic receives the committee output and can lower confidence or veto with explicit counter-evidence; its effect is recorded separately.
Agent timeout: the agent is cancelled, recorded as an error with latency, and the committee completes with the remaining agents.
Agent raising or returning schema-invalid output is isolated; the decision log records the error and the ensemble excludes it.
Every decision is persisted and traceable: input snapshot id, model, prompt version, output, latency, errors and downstream ensemble result.
GET /api/v1/agents/decisions returns the decision log with filtering by instrument, agent and time.
Replaying the same snapshots through the committee with the mock LLM yields identical ensemble decisions.
Agent Decision Log page shows each agent's input snapshot, output, probability, evidence, disagreement, latency, errors and model/version.

Anthropic client builds requests per the current official SDK (model id, structured output format, no forced tool choice, no deprecated thinking parameters) - verified against recorded request fixtures.
Recorded Anthropic responses parse into the typed schemas; refusal and max_tokens stop reasons are handled before content is read.
Budget control: per-call max tokens and timeout; the daily USD cap is enforced from token usage and model pricing; when exceeded the client refuses calls and agents abstain.
Token and cost usage are recorded per call and exported as metrics by agent and model.
The API key is never logged, never included in errors, and never sent anywhere except the provider host; LLM is disabled by default.
Prompts are versioned; the prompt version and model id are stored with every decision; changing a prompt changes its version hash.
Untrusted content (news, filings) is delimited; an injected instruction inside content does not change the output schema or produce actions; outputs citing unknown sources are rejected.
LLM API 429/5xx/timeout: bounded retries per the SDK policy, then a typed abstain; the committee completes.
LLM returns malformed or schema-invalid output: rejected, logged, agent abstains; no partial data reaches the ensemble.
Opt-in live test with a real API key: one structured call returns a schema-valid signal within budget. Excluded from default runs.
Market orders fill at the opposite quote side after latency (buy at ask, sell at bid) plus modelled slippage.
Limit orders fill only when the market trades through the limit; price improvement on gaps; no fill at the touch with bar data.
Stop and stop-limit orders trigger correctly; gap-through-stop fills at the worse post-gap price, not the stop price.
Partial fills respect the volume-participation cap and displayed size; remaining quantity keeps working.
Order rejection: closed market, halted or delisted instrument, below minimum notional, unsupported TIF, insufficient buying power, short without borrow.
Cost model: commissions, spread, slippage, borrow fees and funding are itemised per fill and total correctly in currency and bps.
Latency model: no fill occurs at or before the timestamp of the data that triggered the decision.
Market hours: no fills while closed, DAY orders expire at the session close, early closes and holidays honoured, crypto fills on weekends.
Corporate actions: split, reverse split, cash dividend and delisting adjust positions, working orders and cash correctly.
Stale working orders are cancelled/expired at their maximum age.
Order state machine: only legal transitions are possible; terminal states are final; every transition is recorded.
Lookahead guard: perturbing data after time t never changes decisions or fills up to t; no fill timestamp is <= its decision timestamp.
Accounting invariants: cash + position value changes equal the sum of fills and costs; filled quantity never exceeds order quantity.
A backtest with the same data snapshot, parameters and seed reproduces identical trades and statistics.
Closing-price rule: a strategy cannot use a bar's close to fill an order within that bar unless it declares the close-auction timing model, which is recorded in run metadata.
Chronological train/test split and walk-forward windows never overlap in a way that leaks test data into training.
Performance statistics (return, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, max drawdown, hit rate, profit factor, exposure, turnover) match hand-computed golden values.
Parameter-stability analysis, benchmark comparison and bootstrap confidence intervals are computed deterministically from a seed.
A multiple-hypothesis warning is attached when a parameter search exceeds the configured number of trials.
Each run persists code version, data snapshot id, parameters, provider, date range, cost model, random seed and results; runs are retrievable by id.
Data snapshots are immutable Parquet sets identified by content hash and queryable with DuckDB.
Strategy Lab: configure a backtest (ranges, costs), run it, and view performance, benchmark, drawdown, rolling performance, trade distribution and parameter sensitivity with text alternatives.
Hard rule: stale, malformed, quarantined or below-minimum-quality execution-critical data rejects with DATA_INTEGRITY.
Hard rule: invalid, missing or stale account balance rejects with ACCOUNT_INVALID.
Hard rule: duplicate order (same client_order_id or equivalent open order) rejects with DUPLICATE_ORDER.
Hard rule: maximum account gross/net exposure.
Hard rule: configured max daily drawdown blocks new risk but allows risk-reducing exits.
Hard rule: per-symbol hard cap.
Hard rule: impossible stop or size (wrong side, non-positive, too tight, zero quantity after rounding, below minimum lot).
Hard rule: market closed / instrument halted or delisted.
Hard rule: broker disconnected or unknown state during an exposure-changing order rejects with BROKER_UNSAFE.
Kill switch: BLOCK_NEW_RISK and BLOCK_ALL semantics; state persists across restart; changes are audited.
Each soft multiplier (confidence, liquidity, regime, disagreement, correlation, event) is monotonic, bounded in [floor, 1] and can only reduce size.
Soft factors alone never produce zero size: the global floor applies and SOFT_FLOOR_REACHED is reported.
Sizing formula golden cases: risk_budget, base_qty from stop distance, multipliers, rounding down to the quantity increment.
Caps: max notional, symbol exposure, sector/theme exposure, gross/net exposure, remaining portfolio risk and participation each bind correctly and record their effect.
RiskConfig validation rejects values outside the hard bounds; there is no unbounded or Kelly-fraction sizing path.
Property: final quantity never exceeds any cap, is never negative, and never exceeds base quantity.
Property: identical inputs always give identical RiskDecision (determinism).
Portfolio accounting: cash, positions, realised/unrealised P&L, gross/net exposure and concentration match golden scenarios including fees.
Historical-simulation VaR and expected shortfall at 95%/99% match golden values; insufficient history is reported, not estimated silently.
Every evaluation persists a RiskDecision with rule results, multipliers, caps and reason codes; decision metrics are exported.
Portfolio/Risk page shows cash, positions, P&L, exposures, correlation, VaR/ES with stated limitations, risk budget, drawdown and concentration; mobile risk overview works.
Paper broker submits, acknowledges, partially fills, fills, cancels and rejects orders through the shared state machine.
Idempotent submission: the same client_order_id never creates two orders; a submit timeout is resolved by lookup, not re-send.
Duplicate order acknowledgements and duplicate fill reports are no-ops; out-of-order fills are applied correctly.
Mode safety: research mode rejects all orders; paper never routes to a live endpoint; the paper adapter refuses a non-paper base URL; live mode cannot start without every gate.
Fail closed: an instrument whose required feed is unhealthy, stale or below minimum quality cannot receive new risk-increasing orders; working entry orders are cancelled; protective stops remain.
Reconciliation detects position/order mismatches with the broker, engages BLOCK_NEW_RISK and raises an alert.
Broker rejection is surfaced with a classified reason and leaves portfolio state unchanged.
Broker disconnect mid-order: state becomes unknown, new risk is blocked, reconnect reconciles without duplicate orders.
Alpaca paper trading API fixtures (order, order update stream, account, positions, error envelopes) parse and map to the canonical order model.
Authentication: Argon2id password hashing, server-side sessions, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies, idle timeout, rotation on login, rate-limited login.
Every state-changing endpoint requires an authenticated session, the correct role, a valid CSRF token and an allowed Origin.
Audit log records logins, order lifecycle, risk decisions, kill-switch and configuration changes; the application role cannot update or delete audit rows.
Private WebSocket channels (orders, portfolio) require an authenticated session.
End-to-end paper flow: ensemble decision -> order intent -> risk decision -> order -> fills -> position -> attribution record.
Post-trade attribution compares expected edge and costs with realised results and feeds forecast error to the reliability tracker.
Order Blotter shows submitted, acknowledged, partial, filled, rejected and cancelled orders with timestamps and broker ids; updates live.
Post-Trade Attribution page shows expected edge, realised result, signal contribution, cost difference, execution quality and forecast error.
Paper-mode banner is always visible in paper mode; order entry is impossible in research mode.
Alpaca market-data fixtures (bars, trades, quotes, stream messages, errors) map to canonical observations; IEX is labelled REALTIME_SINGLE_VENUE and delayed SIP DELAYED with delay_seconds=900.
FX/reference provider fixtures map to canonical observations with the weakest plausible feed quality and correct pip precision.
Each new adapter passes the shared provider conformance suite and the failure-injection suite.
Corporate actions ingestion: splits, reverse splits and dividends are stored and applied to adjusted series; raw series stay unadjusted.
Symbol changes and delistings: history follows the instrument id; delisted instruments stop streaming and are flagged.
Trading halts: a halted instrument is flagged, bars are not fabricated during the halt, and execution is blocked.
Equity bars respect regular/pre/post sessions; no bar spans the overnight gap.
yfinance (if enabled) is labelled UNOFFICIAL, is off by default, and cannot be selected as an execution-critical source.
Command Center shows crypto, equity and FX overviews with per-asset-class market status and correct feed badges.
SEC EDGAR fixtures (submissions, company facts, frames) parse into typed filing/event models.
SEC client sends the declared User-Agent, stays at or below 10 requests/second and backs off when throttled.
FRED fixtures parse; copyrighted series are flagged; the required FRED notice is attached to responses that include FRED data.
CFTC COT fixtures parse; report-date vs release-date are distinguished so data is never used before its release time.
ECB reference-rate fixtures parse and are labelled EOD reference data.
Event model: timestamp, source, symbol, category, relevance, optional sentiment, link/provenance; point-in-time availability is enforced (no use before publication).
GET /api/v1/news and /events return items with provenance links, filtering and pagination.
News/Events page lists items with timestamp, source, symbol, category, relevance, sentiment where applicable and a provenance link; scheduled events appear on the Command Center.
Pairs/stat-arb: cointegration test, hedge ratio and spread z-score are computed on training data only and applied out of sample.
Time-aware cross-validation (purged/embargoed splits) never places a training sample after a validation sample it could leak into.
Feature-leakage test: labels are constructed strictly from future returns and never included in features; a planted leak is detected.
Probability calibration (reliability curve, Brier score) is computed out of sample; an uncalibrated model is flagged.
Model acceptance gate: a model is rejected unless it beats the simple-rule benchmark out of sample with stability across windows; training accuracy alone never qualifies.
Interpretable baselines (logistic regression, linear, tree) train reproducibly from a seed and record data snapshot and feature versions.
RL/FinRL-style experiments are flagged research-only and cannot be registered as a production signal source.
Walk-forward ML evaluation persists per-window metrics and the model card; results are reproducible.
Built web bundle contains no secret and no non-public environment variable.
Inbound rate limiting on API routes (strict on login and order endpoints) returns 429 with Retry-After.
Content-Security-Policy, HSTS and frame-ancestors are enforced in the prod profile; containers run as non-root.
Database roles: the application role has no DDL rights and no UPDATE/DELETE on the audit log.
Backup and restore of PostgreSQL round-trips state; documented in the runbook.
Load test: the stream pipeline sustains the target message rate without unbounded queue growth; queue depth metrics stay bounded.
Tracing: a request produces correlated spans across API, provider call and database when tracing is enabled.
Chaos run: random provider disconnects, DB and Redis restarts during streaming leave the system consistent and recover without manual action.
Full prod-profile compose stack builds, starts, passes health checks and the cross-stack smoke script.
Full regression: every page passes its e2e and axe checks on desktop, tablet and mobile viewports.
